clue.text: Toffee made by bishop, say, with whisky

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for a bishop
to say something is to utter it
Scotch is whisky distilled in Scotland

explanation.surface: A sweet concocted by a clergyman with a dash of whisky in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bishop, say' reads as one idea, a bishop for example, but it splits into B and the verb UTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard brittle sweet of boiled sugar and butter, a kind of toffee.

clue.text: Be without one sketch of an aircraft

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word be wraps round what follows

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
a plan is a sketch or drawing of a design

explanation.surface: An instruction to go without a single drawing of a flying machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: BE goes round I and PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A biplane is an early type of aeroplane with two pairs of wings.

clue.text: Earnest dedication?

definitions.meaning: an earnest is a pledge or payment given as a sign of more to come
a dedication in a book is a small sign of the author's regard

explanation.definitionFit: Both an earnest payment and a book's dedication are symbols or pledges standing for something larger.

clue.text: Bound to hit the ambassador in the end

indicators.note: the swatting and the ambassador sit inside the word for the end

parts.note: the end is simply END
to swat is to hit sharply
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: Someone is destined to strike the ambassador eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'destined', but it is the past tense of bind, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enswathed is to be wrapped or swaddled, that is tied up in bandages.

clue.text: Fish caught in unhappy circumstances

indicators.note: the letter for caught is placed within the word for unhappy

parts.note: circumstances that are unhappy are sad ones
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A fish is landed while things are going badly.
explanation.definitionFit: The scad is a sea fish, also called horse mackerel.

clue.text: Scion unattracted by a hunting expedition

parts.note: to be off something is to have lost one's liking for it
a shoot is a party out hunting game with guns

explanation.surface: A young heir is unimpressed by the idea of a day's hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scion' suggests a young aristocrat, but it is the gardener's sense of a shoot from a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A scion is a cutting or side growth of a plant, so a branch growing off the main stem.

clue.text: Cringe like many a debtor

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
a debtor is one who owes money, an ower

explanation.surface: To shrink back in fear, as plenty of people in debt do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' is a link; 'many' gives C, the Roman hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to crouch or shrink in fear, the same as to cringe.

clue.text: Damaged what, in the Cape, is a prickly tree

indicators.note: the jumbled word sits inside the name of the Cape

parts.note: Cape Horn, at the tip of South America, is often called simply the Horn

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of shape and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A thorny tree in the Cape region has been harmed somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damaged' makes WTHA of the letters in 'what', and 'in' puts that inside HORN.
explanation.definitionFit: The hawthorn is a thorny hedgerow shrub or small tree with red berries called haws.

clue.text: Bogus means of communication an unknown quantity

parts.note: a telephone is a way of talking at a distance
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: A fake telephone line connects to some mysterious amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoney is informal for fake or not genuine, which is what bogus means.

clue.text: Quiet employees take in president — it's perfectly plain

indicators.note: the employees, with quiet in front, absorb the president

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly
a company's staff are its employees
Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: Silent staff admit the president, and everything is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the idiom 'as plain as a pikestaff', meaning quite obvious; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obvious is said to be as plain as a pikestaff, the long wooden shaft of a pike.

clue.text: Apparition one dismissed in such indignation

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so the letter for one goes from the ghost

parts.note: a wraith is a ghost or apparition
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A ghost, sent packing, is furious about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrath is fierce anger, close kin to indignation.

clue.text: Make tough boy put girl first

indicators.note: the girl's name is told to go at the front, ahead of the boy's

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
Al is a boy's name, short for Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: A command to a lad to let a young woman go ahead of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' is a link: the boy's name AL comes after ANNE because the girl goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Annealing metal or glass by heating and slow cooling makes it tougher and less brittle.

clue.text: He made chairs for a woman, put to use outside

indicators.note: the words for put to use go round the woman

parts.note: a chair that is sat on has been put to use
her is a pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A craftsman built seats for a lady, and they were used by others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. SAT ON fits the chairs of the definition as a nice touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was an 18th-century English furniture designer famous for elegant chairs.

clue.text: They, are endlessly, represented 'as unrefined

indicators.note: represented means presented afresh, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly means the word are loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Some people are perpetually portrayed as coarse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts 'are' to AR; 'represented' shuffles THEY plus AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse or crude, so lacking refinement.

clue.text: Thin and upset if a long time in debt

indicators.note: the overturned words are placed within the word for debt

parts.note: being in the red means being in debt

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Thin and distressed because I owe money for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IF and ERA to make AREFI, which 'in' places inside RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarefied air is thin, with less density than usual.

clue.text: Drudge grips trunk

parts.note: a dog is a mechanical clamp or gripping device
the trunk is the body without head or limbs

explanation.surface: A menial worker clutches a large box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grips' looks like a verb, but it is a plural noun: dogs are gripping tools.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogsbody is someone given all the menial jobs, a drudge.

clue.text: Tip 23, perhaps, and odd characters from Paris

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters may be ordered some other way

parts.note: a cross-reference to the answer of 23 across

indicators.note: the first, third and fifth letters of Paris are taken

explanation.surface: A rubbish dump, possibly, with a few strange people from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is APACHE; 'odd characters from' Paris gives PRS, and 'perhaps' shuffles all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is British for a rubbish dump, which is what a scrapheap is.

clue.text: Party programme for a thick soul, say

definitions.meaning: a political party's set of policies
soul sounds like sole, and a thick sole on a shoe is a raised base

explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals the pun: soul sounds like sole, and shoes with thick soles are platform shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's manifesto of policies is its platform, and so is a raised thick-soled shoe base.

clue.text: Excellent 'new leader with a 15?

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords

indicators.note: new means made over afresh, so the word leader is rearranged

explanation.surface: Is the outstanding fresh boss together with a lackey?
explanation.walkthrough: 15 across is DOGSBODY, read here as dog's body: an Airedale has one.
explanation.definitionFit: An Airedale is a large terrier, so it has the body of a dog.

clue.text: As. proof, quote some of the Sadducees

indicators.note: only part of the word Sadducees is needed, the run inside it

explanation.surface: A scholar cites a passage from the Sadducees as evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To adduce is to cite something as evidence in support of an argument.

clue.text: University managed by America is heaven personified

parts.note: to run something is to manage it

explanation.surface: A college run by the Americans is paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Uranus was the god embodying the sky.

clue.text: Exudation to observe on one side of a leaf

parts.note: to see is to observe
a page is one side of a leaf of paper in a book

explanation.surface: Sap oozing out to be watched on one face of a plant's leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaf' suggests a plant, but it is a leaf of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is liquid slowly oozing out, an exudation.

clue.text: Exact description of the article

definitions.meaning: in grammar 'the' is called this kind of article

explanation.definitionFit: Definite means precise, and 'the' is the definite article in grammar.

clue.text: PM appearing at the end of 12

definitions.meaning: Lord ... was British Prime Minister from 1770 to 1782
on a clock face set like a compass, a hand pointing to twelve points to the top

explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like afternoon, but it is a Prime Minister. A clock hand ending at 12 points up, the compass direction at the top of a map.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord North was a British premier, and the twelve on a clock face sits at the compass top.

clue.text: Indian quickly restraining horse's head

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so the quick word surrounds the letter

parts.note: apace means quickly

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Native American swiftly reins in a horse by its head.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a Native American people, an older sense of Indian.

clue.text: Fashion? That's for an attractive girl.

parts.note: the cut of clothes is their style or fashion
i.e., from Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Is style the key to looking pretty?
explanation.definitionFit: Cutie is informal for an attractive or endearing young woman.

clue.text: Pearl's mother 'beheaded in a Brazilian state?

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: nacre is mother-of-pearl

explanation.surface: Was a woman's mother decapitated somewhere in Brazil?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pearl' looks like a woman's name, but mother-of-pearl is nacre.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre is a state in the far west of Brazil.

clue.text: In which signals need no decoding

definitions.text: In which signals need no decoding

parts.words: In which signals need no decoding
parts.note: a message sent in plain language rather than in cipher is said to be sent in this way

explanation.definitionFit: A message sent in clear is in plain language, not in code.

clue.text: Its work is noted in the pit

definitions.text: Its work is noted in the pit

parts.words: Its work is noted in the pit
parts.note: players in a theatre's sunken pit read music written in notes

explanation.definitionFit: A theatre's band of instrumental players sits in the pit and plays from written music.

clue.text: Upon which he thought he' saw a Buffalo (Carroll)

definitions.text: Upon which he thought he' saw a Buffalo (Carroll)

parts.words: Upon which he thought he' saw a Buffalo (Carroll)
parts.note: a line from the Mad Gardener's Song in Lewis Carroll's Sylvie and Bruno

explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's gardener thought he saw a Buffalo upon the mantelpiece over the fireplace.
